theme_type.description: Which family this themebook belongs to. Required and without a default: a themebook with no type prints the wrong banner and the wrong erosion track.

keywords.description: The handful of words the themebook prints to say at a glance what it is about.

items.description: One keyword printed on the themebook's header.

introduction.description: The opening paragraph of the themebook, which pitches the theme to the player. Supports Markdown.

concept.description: The one-line concept, which says what a character built on this themebook is.
examples: You are who you are, and that is enough.

power_tag_questions.description: The lettered questions whose answers become power tags, in printed order.

letter.description: The letter the books print beside the question. It travels onto the played card, where it identifies which question a tag answers.

text.description: The question itself, written as the themebook prints it. Supports inline Markdown.
examples: What is the one thing you are best at?
What do you carry that no one else would recognise?

examples.description: The suggested answers the books print under the question, as a prompt rather than a constraint.

items.description: One suggested answer, printed in the margin.
One lettered question of the themebook, which a player answers with a tag.

power_tag_rule.description: How many power questions are answered, and how they are chosen.

required_count.description: How many questions must be answered, whichever the player would rather pick. The first power question is usually required.

chosen_count.description: How many further questions the player picks freely from the list.

note.description: Anything the counts cannot say, written as the themebook says it.
examples: Answer the first question, then two more of your choice.
One extra power tag costs one extra weakness tag.

weakness_tag_questions.description: The lettered questions whose answers become weakness tags, in printed order.

letter.description: The letter the books print beside the question. It travels onto the played card, where it identifies which question a tag answers.

text.description: The question itself, written as the themebook prints it. Supports inline Markdown.
examples: What is the one thing you are best at?
What do you carry that no one else would recognise?

examples.description: The suggested answers the books print under the question, as a prompt rather than a constraint.

items.description: One suggested answer, printed in the margin.
One lettered question of the themebook, which a player answers with a tag.

weakness_tag_rule.description: How many weakness questions are answered, and how they are chosen.

required_count.description: How many questions must be answered, whichever the player would rather pick. The first power question is usually required.

chosen_count.description: How many further questions the player picks freely from the list.

note.description: Anything the counts cannot say, written as the themebook says it.
examples: Answer the first question, then two more of your choice.
One extra power tag costs one extra weakness tag.

extra_tags.description: Tags the themebook hands out directly, without a question to answer.

items.description: One tag the themebook grants outside its questions.

motivation.description: The motivation zone. A Crew themebook leaves it out and prints its crew relationships instead.

kind.description: Whether this zone is written as a Mystery, as an Identity, or left to the player.

intro.description: The line the themebook prints above the zone, which tells the player what to write. Supports inline Markdown.
examples: What is the question you cannot stop asking?
Write the statement you keep proving to yourself.

examples.description: The suggested motivations printed with the zone.

options.description: A closed list to pick from, for the themebooks that offer one instead of a blank line.

items.description: One motivation the player picks from a closed list.

rule.description: What answering or abandoning the motivation does, when the themebook spells it out.
examples: When you answer this Mystery, the theme fades and you lose it.

title_guidance.description: What the themebook tells the player to write on the card's title line.
examples: Name the part of yourself this theme is about.

crew_relationships.description: The situations a Crew themebook asks the table to answer for. Empty on every other theme type.

scenario.description: The situation the crew themebook asks the players to answer for.
examples: When one of us is arrested,
When we disagree on where the money goes,

outcome.description: What that situation does to the crew.

items.description: One crew relationship, which a Crew themebook prints in place of a motivation.

improvements.description: The five improvements a theme built here can buy. Every themebook the books print carries five, no more and no fewer.

name.description: The improvement's title, as the themebook prints it.

effect.description: What buying the improvement does. Supports inline Markdown.
examples: Take an additional power tag for this theme.
Unlock a custom move for this theme.

items.description: One improvement a player can buy for a theme built here.

meta.description: Attribution and cataloging fields for the themebook's origin.

publication_type.description: Classifies the themebook's source to aid cataloging and tooling.

source.description: Source title (book, supplement, PDF) where this themebook appears.

authors.description: List of credited authors or contributors.

page.description: Page number (if relevant to the source).

description: City of Mist - a themebook: the blank questionnaire a player fills in to build a theme, not the answers they write. The filled card is the separate `theme-card` target. Note that there is no Mist theme type in City of Mist; that notion belongs to Legend in the Mist.
